description: Hello! we are the "taare Zameen par" a group of college students who are interested in space exploration, web development and creativity!
summary: Jezero Atlas is an interactive web map to assist astronauts in planning a Marswalk around Jezero Crater. It brings together a range of NASA data (orbital imagery, MOLA elevation and slope, thermal inertia, atmospheric conditions) into a single view. Hazard overlays indicate sand traps and slopes over 15 degrees, and the 3D terrain flyover gives you a sense of what the ground actually looks like to ensure it's safe for an astronaut. [Science walk through Neretva Vallis with science stops, turn-back point and retreat path.] All values are labelled as measured, modelled or simulated. It's a way of combining a number of different mission datasets into a single hyperlocal view that the astronaut can use to select a safe path to a science target. Safety first: hazards and weather are right next to the route. The first people to walk on Mars will need much more than a regional map. It's going to take all of our knowledge, all of our imagination and all of our hard work to become an interplanetary species. Tools such as this will help the first astronauts get to the science sites they want to visit quickly and get back safely.
details:
1. What Does It Do & How Does It Work?

Jezero Atlas is an interactive, browser-based Planetary Operations & Mission Planning Platform covering a 500 km radius around Jezero Crater on Mars.

  • Procedural + Orbital Digital Elevation Model (DEM): On initialization, the platform computes a 512×512512 \times 512512×512 planetary grid calibrated to Mars's mean radius. It models major regional features—including the Jezero basin, Isidis Planitia lowlands, Syrtis Major volcanic shield, Nili Fossae tectonic grabens, and ancient river valleys (Neretva, Sava, and Pliva Valles)—and calculates geodesic slope gradients, barometric scale-height surface pressure, dust optical depth, and thermal inertia.
  • Live Orbital Tile Streaming: When online, it streams live Web Map Tile Service (WMTS) mosaics from NASA’s Mars Trek (Mars_Viking_MDIM21_ClrMosaic_global_232m) directly onto the HTML5 2D Canvas, layered seamlessly with procedural elevation contours and slope hazard masks.
  • A Pathfinding & Route Optimizer: Users can place waypoints or select Point A and Point B to generate traverse routes. An integrated A grid pathfinder* evaluates terrain slopes and penalizes inclines exceeding. It offers two optimization modes:
    1. Safest Optimal Path: Avoids steep crater rims and graben scarps.
    2. Safest + Shortest + Top 3 Science Targets: Automatically routes past high priority astrobiological/geological sites (e.g., clay deltas, carbonate belts) while maintaining safe slope corridors.
  • 1-Sol Astronomical Day/Night Simulation: Simulates the solar terminator across a full Martian soil dynamically calculating solar elevation, azimuth, and day/night shadow progression.
  • 3D WebGL Flyover & Multi-Window HUD: Uses Three.js to render an interactive 3D heightmap mesh with adjustable vertical exaggeration (4x, 8x, 16x), housed inside a custom GPU-accelerated (translate3d) movable, resizable, and collapsible window manager.

2. What Benefits Does It Have?

  • Zero-Backend Accessibility: Built entirely in a single self-contained HTML file with no server dependencies, allowing mission planners, researchers, or students to run complex planetary GIS analysis directly in any desktop or mobile browser.
  • Multi-Sensor Data Fusion: Lets operators switch instantaneously between six analytical lenses—Satellite Mosaic, Simplified Biome/Province, MOLA Elevation, THEMIS Thermal Inertia, Atmospheric Column, and Slope Gradient—without losing spatial context.
  • Mission-Ready Export: Planned traverses and elevation profiles can be exported immediately as industry-standard .GeoJSON (for QGIS/ArcGIS) or .CSV telemetry tables.
  • Multi-Device Adaptive UI: Includes a built-in deployment switcher that adapts the interface for Habitat Command (Dark Obsidian/Cobalt), Rugged Field Tablet (High-legibility Light mode), and Spacesuit Visor HUD (High-contrast emerald night-vision palette).

3. What Is the Intended Impact of the Project?

  • Human & Robotic Traverse Safety: By automatically flagging slopes and estimating travel durations, the tool helps prevent rover rollover/slip hazards and accounts for the metabolic exertion limits of astronauts wearing pressurized spacesuits during Extravehicular Activities (EVAs).
  • In-Situ Resource Utilization (ISRU) Planning: Maps six critical Martian mineral and resource groups (hydrated smectite clays, Mg/Fe carbonates, olivine, opaline silica, hydrated sulfates/subsurface ice candidates, and Fe/Ti basalt) to support future habitat construction, water extraction, and propellant production.
  • STEM Education & Public Engagement: Bridges complex NASA Planetary Data System (PDS) datasets with an intuitive, game-inspired interface (drawing visual inspiration from Chunkbase), making Mars exploration tangible for students and citizen scientists.

4. Tools, Coding Languages, Hardware & Software Used

  • Languages: HTML5, CSS3, and Vanilla JavaScript (ES6+ with TypedArrays like Float32Array and Uint8Array for high-speed DEM and A* pathfinding math).
  • Graphics & Rendering Engines:
    • HTML5 Canvas 2D API: Custom 60 FPS pan/zoom map renderer, procedural noise/hillshading generator, elevation profile plotter, and offline fallback map previewer.
    • Three.js (r128) / WebGL: Hardware-accelerated 3D terrain mesh flyover viewer.
  • Styling & Typography: Tailwind CSS (via CDN), CSS Custom Properties (design tokens), Inter, and JetBrains Mono.
  • Data Sources & APIs: NASA Mars Trek WMTS Tile Server, NASA/JPL Photojournal (PIA rover & HiRISE orbital imagery), MOLA (Mars Orbiter Laser Altimeter), THEMIS, MRO CRISM, Perseverance MEDA, and MSL Curiosity RAD reference datasets.
  • Target Hardware: Cross-platform responsive design supporting desktop workstations (mouse + wheel), rugged field tablets (multi-touch pinch-to-zoom and pointer-capture window dragging/resizing), and visor displays.

5. How Is My Project Creative?

  • "Chunkbase-Meets-NASA Mission Control" Aesthetic: Instead of cluttered, intimidating GIS software, it combines a clean, segmented Chunkbase-style navigation bar and biome-style terrain views with an aerospace heads-up display (HUD).
  • Dual Shape + Color Resource Encoding: Every resource deposit is encoded with both a distinct color and a unique geometric glyph (● Clays, ◆ Carbonates, ▲ Olivine, ⬡ Silica, ■ Sulfates/Ice, ★ Fe/Ti Basalt) so overlays remain legible even over complex elevation heatmaps or for color-vision-deficient users.
  • Interactive Core & Deep Space Network (DSN) Simulator: Goes beyond surface mapping by letting users inspect actual Perseverance drill core stratigraphy (Robine, Wildcat Ridge, Mayaro, Sapphire Canyon) and test Earth-Mars one-way light-time communication delays (333 to 222222 minutes).
  • Resilient Offline Map Fallback: If external NASA/JPL image servers are unreachable, the rover imagery viewer dynamically renders a custom mini-radar/contour sector preview (drawRoverMapPreview) on an HTML5 <canvas> so the UI never displays a broken image icon.

6. What Factors Did My Team Consider?

  • Scientific Honesty & Data Limitations: The platform explicitly distinguishes between confirmed observations and modelled estimates—for example, noting that because Perseverance does not carry an ionizing radiation dosimeter, baseline radiation numbers are calibrated to MSL Curiosity RAD measurements at Gale Crater, and atmospheric readouts are barometric scale-height estimates rather than live telemetry.
  • Human Factors & EVA Biomechanics: Incorporated a dedicated NASA HRP (Human Research Program) biomechanics module accounting for Mars's gravity, spacesuit joint torque resistance (which increases metabolic exertion by inclines, PLSS cooling capacity, and oxygen consumption.
  • Performance & Mobile Ergonomics: Used GPU-composited transform: translate3d() for smooth 60 FPS window dragging, pointer-capture events (setPointerCapture) for reliable touch resizing, minimum 36px touch targets on mobile viewports, and cached offscreen raster buffers so switching map layers is instantaneous.
